label: Mass-casualty incident

extra_patients.citation: Brunner J et al. (2014) Radiology 273(1):78-87: 40 patients presented to Brigham and Women's Hospital after the 2013 Boston Marathon bombing (16 admitted, 24 discharged, 10 emergent operations, no deaths). Upper bound: Lake CK (2025) Trauma Surg Acute Care Open 10:e001786: the 2017 Las Vegas shooting injured over 800 people, 413 with gunshot wounds needing immediate treatment, spread over the city's hospitals, mostly self-transported.
extra_patients.note: One hospital's share of one urban bombing; a city-wide event of the Las Vegas size can send a few hundred to the nearest hospital. Second URL: https://doi.org/10.1136/tsaco-2025-001786

window_min.citation: Brunner J et al. (2014) Radiology 273(1):78-87: median time from blast to patient arrival at the hospital 97 min (IQR 43-139) for the 40 Boston Marathon bombing patients.
window_min.note: DERIVED: an inter-quartile spread of 96 min implies arrivals spread over roughly three hours, not 90 minutes. Self-transported casualties (Las Vegas 2017) arrive faster and unannounced: use the low end for that scenario.
